newsitem.title: TURKEY: Israel's Levy to talk trade, Mideast peace in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Levy to talk trade, Mideast peace in Turkey.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy will discuss ways to boost trade and brief Turkey on the stalled Middle East peace process in a two-day visit to Ankara next week, an Israeli official said on Saturday.
"The visit has political and economic aspects," said the official, who declined to be named.
"His visit comes only days after the Turkish parliament ratified the Israeli-Turkish free trade accord on Friday," he told Reuters.

This is the first high-level visit since both countries formed new governments last summer. Levy will have talks with Turkish ministers and officials on investments and joint ventures in both countries, he said.

Levy, accompanied by Israeli businessmen, is scheduled to meet President Suleyman Demirel, Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller and state ministers Ufuk Soylemez and Ayfer Yilmaz on the April 8-9 visit he said.
But his meeting with predominantly Moslem but secular Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has not yet been confirmed, he said.
"If there is not a meeting Levy will regret it. But we already have good relations and one meeting will not be able to set back the relations," he said.
Relations between the two countries have been cemented by two military accords sealed last year.

The accords, condemned by Iran, many in the Arab world and some Islamists in Turkey, allow Israeli jets on training flights to use Turkish airspace and for Israel to upgrade Turkish airforce F-4 jets.
Since becoming prime minister of the coalition government with conservatives last June, Erbakan has toned down his criticism of closer relations with Israel.

"(Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu sent a letter to Erbakan when he was elected prime minister. He said there is still room for a dialogue despite difference of views. Levy will come with the same message," the Israeli official said.
"Only a dialogue can solve differences of opinion," he said.

He said Levy would also discuss the Middle East peace process, which is in turmoil after construction of an Israeli settlement in Arab East Jerusalem sparked more than two weeks of clashes between Israeli troops and Palestinian protesters
"Turkey, as a balanced country, has good relations with both sides, Israelis and Palestinians," he said.

Israel and Turkey will revive plans to sell Turkish water from the southern river of Managvat to Israel and other countries, he said. A Turkish project to build a water treatment plant on the river is underway.
"The two sides will also launch joint economic committee meetings," the official said.
The bilateral free trade accord envisages bringing Turkey's trade with Israel in harmony with Ankara's pledges to the European Union, with which it launched a customs union in 1996.
It also paves the way for Turkey to raise its trade with the United States, Canada and central America through Israel, which has preferred trade ties with those countries.
